compensating.why: hop 2 prefers the any-setter field over the any-setter method
hop 3 returns field accessors without verification
hop 4 also accepts accessors whose raw type is Object

context_edits.old: private Throwable throwOrReturnThrowable(Throwable t, DeserializationContext ctxt)

expected_signature: first argument not of type String or Object, but java.lang.Object
ownership_reason: Only the gold decides whether an accessor that carries the any-setter annotation can be used: hops 1 and 3 pass the collected properties or the accessor on (returning null when there is none), hop 2 only picks the any-setter method before the any-setter field, and hop 4 only turns the gold's verdict into the accessor or into the original IllegalArgumentException. Whatever a caller does, the gold itself still answers false for an any-setter method whose first parameter is declared as Object, although such a method can receive the bean's unknown properties, which is what the gold's javadoc promises to decide. The convention is pinned outside the gold: BeanDescription.findAnySetterAccessor's javadoc (the method 'needs to take 2 arguments, first one String or Object'); StdKeyDeserializer.forType, where String, Object and CharSequence keys all take the JSON property name as is, and MapDeserializer._isStdKeyDeser, where String or Object raw key types use the default key handling ('JSON String becomes Java String'), with MapDeserializationTest testUntypedMap2 (Object keys of a raw HashMap receive the property names) passing; BeanDeserializerFactory.constructAnySetter, the production caller, builds the any-setter property from the method's first parameter type resolved through the bean's type bindings; AnySetterTest testSimpleMapImitation (String-keyed method), AnySetterTest testJsonAnySetterOnMap (Map field) and POJOPropertiesCollectorTest testJackson744 (the any-setter method is located) pass on the variant. Hop 4's message also names the accepted key types (String or Object).
